comments.value: Regarding banner cropping, it would be nice to post a location for group owners to choose where to crop the banner, including on the official website, below the in-game player ID.

The group banner that appears above user nameplates has unexpected scaling behaviour. 

The image in the banner is scaling to accomodate for different nameplate lengths. It is scaling by anchoring the bottom edge and moving the top edge. This is unexpected because it offsets the center point of the image, causing content to become cut off.

You can verify this by using a square aspect UV Checker Texture.

comments.mergedPostDetails:
[#1 screen is a third person view.]

The text on the banner image itself is perfectly centered, but in the UI it's offset lower. When you open your Quick Menu and full nameplates show up the banner gets offset higher.

[#2 screen is first person view.]

The banner centering looks correct when looking at your own nameplate, but its background is set as transparent and it just looks weird with how the cropped corners are stil there and the user icon overlaps the banner.

I generally like the group feature.

The banner above the nameplate was one of the things that seemed particularly attractive to me when I was experimenting with the group feature.

By the way, I noticed an issue when I was trying out the banner with my friends. By the way, there is an issue that I noticed when I was experimenting with the banner with my fellow members.

1. there is a difference between the banner over my head and the banner over someone else's head. I believe this is probably due to the fact that the reference position for displaying the banner is not standardized.

2. In cases where the status message is somewhat long, the expansion rate of the banner increases. This is when the ESC menu is not displayed; if the status message is long, the nameplate also stretches long, and I wonder if this is the cause.

I would like the group banner to always look the same no matter who is looking at whom. We look forward to the development of this new endeavor. Thank you.
